````markdown
# M10 — Loop Prompts

_Live end-to-end Kaggle regression test on
[Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/tpu-getting-started)._
_For sequential, partly autonomous execution on Arch Linux._
_Prerequisite: M9 exit confirmed (live LB recorded, dry-run e2e green; see `docs/m9-final-review.md`)._
_Shared rules: every Loop Prompt below MUST follow `docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md` (sequencing, no real Kaggle/Anthropic outside designated approval paths, DB DSN + sandbox bypass, **per-milestone worktree by default**, secret denylist)._

---

## M10 at a glance

M10 is the **second end-to-end live Kaggle regression** for this platform, and
the first to exercise the **notebook-submission / kernel-push** path.
M9 validated the CSV-submission path (`kca kaggle submit` →
`kaggle competitions submit`) on Spaceship Titanic. M10 validates the
notebook-submission path (`kca kaggle push` → `kaggle kernels push` →
kernel run → public LB) on Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU
(`tpu-getting-started`).

Petals to the Metal is "Getting Started" tier: multi-class image
classification over 104 flower species, public leaderboard, no cash prize,
safe for repeated dry-run iteration and a single real kernel push under
explicit human approval. TPU is optional — Kaggle accepts GPU-backed
notebooks for this competition too — so the baseline can run locally
and only the kernel runner needs Kaggle's hardware.

M10 is **not** a leaderboard-chasing milestone. The acceptance criterion is
that the kernel-push loop *runs end-to-end correctly under the approval
gates*, not that the LB score is high. The CV / holdout thresholds in
`docs/milestones.md` §M10 are sanity guards, not targets.

Direct entry into M10 is blocked until **all** are true:

- M9 is merged on main (`docs/m9-final-review.md` exists and reports PASS).
- Issue #11 (dotenv-leak / Kaggle leaderboard pollution) is merged on main —
  hard pre-req for **M10-T007** so the new dry-run e2e test cannot leak
  into the `tpu-getting-started` leaderboard the same way M9 leaked into
  Spaceship Titanic. M10-T000 through M10-T006 may proceed in parallel
  with #11 work; only T007 is gated on it.
- The local Supabase container is running and the M9 DB rows (M9-T002 /
  M9-T004 / M9-T005) are reachable (M10-T006 references the M9 baseline
  for cross-milestone regression sanity).

## GitHub issue / label workflow for M10

Each M10 task is filed as a GitHub issue using the `feature-work.yml` form,
labelled per task type. Issue #12 is the canonical M10 proposal /
decision-confirmation record; individual task issues link back to it.

| Task | Issue labels at file time | Labels added by triage | Labels at merge |
|---|---|---|---|
| M10-T000 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle`, `area:config`, `area:security` | `ai:ready` (after AC + owner) | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T001 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T002 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T003 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:supabase`, `area:ui` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T004 | `type:feature`, `ai:blocked`, `policy:approval-required`, `decision:needed`, `area:kaggle`, `priority:P0` | `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready` only after human comment "approved to push" | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T005 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:worker`, `area:kaggle` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T006 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing` | `ai:ready` | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T007 | `type:test-gap`, `ai:triage`, `area:testing`, `area:ci` | `ai:ready` only after issue #11 is closed | `ai:implementing` → close |
| M10-T008 | `type:feature`, `ai:triage`, `area:release`, `area:docs` | `ai:ready` after T000–T007 closed | `ai:implementing` → close |

T004 is the only task that starts `ai:blocked` and requires a
`decision:confirmed` comment with an explicit "approved to push" record
before triage may promote it to `ai:ready`. This is enforced by the
`github-issue-triage` agent rules in `.claude/skills/github-issue-triage/`.

T007 is the only task gated on closing a separate issue (#11). The
triage agent should refuse to promote T007 to `ai:ready` while
`gh issue view 11 --json state` returns `"OPEN"`.

The PR for each task uses `.github/pull_request_template.md`. The
"Remote side effects" section is load-bearing: T004's PR is the ONLY
M10 PR that may check the "Live Kaggle call" box, and must link the
approval comment from the closing issue.

## Approval gates (summary)

| Gate | When it fires | Where the approval is recorded | Who can approve |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kernel_push` | Worker stages a notebook + kernel-metadata.json and calls into `tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_push` | `human_decisions` row + comment on the closing GitHub issue | Project owner / reviewer named on the issue |
| `kaggle_submit` | Not used in M10 (would be a second-submission path; out of scope) | n/a | n/a |
| `dataset_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |
| `model_upload` | Not used in M10 | n/a | n/a |

The Kaggle approval flow inside M10 is:

```
worker stages notebook + kernel-metadata.json
  → reviewer-gate writes agent_reviews row + agent_job_events
    (target_op="kernel_push")
  → decision_api surfaces pending decision (POST /decisions queued; UI
    reads via supabase-js until issue #15 lands GET /decisions)
  → UI Approval Inbox renders pending decision
  → human approves via UI (POST /decisions/<id>/approve) OR
    `kca decisions approve --id <id>`
  → human comments "approved to push" on the closing issue
  → triage agent promotes issue to `decision:confirmed` + `ai:ready`
  → M10-T004 Loop Prompt runs ONE `kca kaggle push`
  → poll kaggle kernels status until non-running
  → LB score recorded; submissions row written with kernel-run linkage
  → PR opens with the approval comment linked
```

A second real Kaggle push inside M10 is **out of scope**. If a
follow-up experiment in M10-T005 turns out to need its own LB score,
file it as a new M11+ issue and gate it the same way.

## Rollback / stop criteria

Stop the milestone — do **not** advance to the next Loop Prompt — if any of
these is true:

- A real Kaggle kernel push returns an error from Kaggle (rate limit,
  bad notebook metadata, rules violation). The fix path is local:
  regenerate the notebook + kernel metadata and re-request approval;
  do NOT silently retry.
- The reviewer gate (M10-T003) fails to fire when it should, or fires
  when it shouldn't.
- Any `policy:approval-required` issue advances without the corresponding
  `decision:confirmed` label and comment.
- Any test in the validation suite regresses from green to red.
- The DSN, credentials, or `.env*` are accidentally printed in any log,
  audit row, or PR. Stop and rotate the credential immediately.
- Local CV / holdout scores diverge from the M10-T006 thresholds in a
  way that suggests a leakage bug (e.g. holdout near 1.0). Investigate
  before pushing.
- Issue #11 is reopened mid-milestone with evidence that the leak
  re-emerged. Halt T007 work until #11 is green again.

If M10 needs a new architectural decision (e.g. submission-format
auto-selection, a new artifact-storage shape for notebook payloads, a
````

````markdown
# Milestone Loop Protocol

_Shared rules that apply to every milestone Loop Prompt (M0+) unless a
milestone explicitly overrides one._

Each `docs/m*-loop-prompts.md` should reference this file once at the top
rather than duplicating the rules per prompt.

---

## 1. Sequencing

- Loop Prompts within a milestone MUST execute in order.
- Each prompt's **acceptance checks MUST pass** before moving to the next.
- On failure: fix the specific issue and **retry that prompt only**; do
  not skip ahead and do not redo prompts that already passed.

## 2. External systems and side effects

- Do NOT call the **real Anthropic API or Kaggle API** outside of paths
  the milestone explicitly designates as live; default to `--dry-run`.
- Do NOT run real **Kaggle submit / kernel push / dataset upload /
  model upload** unless the milestone explicitly requests it AND a
  human-approval record exists.
- Do NOT change **production Supabase**.

## 3. Database validation

- Use `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:s3cr3t@172.21.0.4:5432/postgres`
  — the `supabase-db` container on the local Docker network.
- Container IPs change on `docker compose down/up`; refresh with:
  ```bash
  docker inspect supabase-db \
    --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}'
  ```
- DB calls and LAN-host calls require `dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true`.
  Cloud LLM calls stay **inside** the sandbox.

## 4. Reporting

- Report **PASS / FAIL / SKIP** inline for each prompt's verification
  step.
- At milestone end, write the milestone's defined **Closeout format**
  (see each milestone's last Loop Prompt for the exact fields).

## 5. Git / GitHub — worktree mode

This project executes each milestone inside a dedicated **git worktree**
branched off `main`.

- **Mid-milestone, mid-prompt:** do not `git commit` or `git push`
  unless the individual task spec explicitly says so. Stage with
  `git add` and surface diffs in the inline report.
- **At milestone end** — once every Loop Prompt has PASSed and the
  milestone's Closeout has been written — Claude Code SHOULD:
  1. `git add` only the files listed in the Closeout's "files changed"
     section (or its equivalent).
  2. `git commit` using either:
     - one squash commit per milestone, OR
     - one commit per Loop Prompt,
     depending on the milestone's preference. The default is **one
     commit per Loop Prompt**, with the milestone's final review as the
     last commit.
  3. `git push` the worktree's branch to the remote.
  4. `gh pr create` against `main` using the milestone's
     `docs/m{N}-final-review.md` as the PR body.

- The following **still require explicit human approval** at any time:
  - `git push --force` (any branch)
  - `gh pr merge` (any PR)
  - any push to `main` directly
  - any `gh label create/edit/delete`, `gh issue edit/comment`,
    `gh pr edit/comment` against issues or PRs **not** owned by this
    milestone

- If the milestone's task spec or scope says
  "do not commit / push / open PRs", that override **wins** — typically
  used for planning-only or evidence-only milestones.

## 6. Secrets and forbidden reads

These are always denied, regardless of milestone:

- `.env*`
- `**/kaggle.json`, `~/.kaggle/kaggle.json`
- `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, any private key contents
- `~/.aws/**`, `~/.config/gcloud/**`
- `secrets/**`

Shell commands that would surface the above (`cat`, `grep`, `head`,
`tail`, `less`, `more`, file uploads) over these paths are blocked at
the hook layer.

---

## How a milestone references this file

In each Loop Prompt block, instead of repeating the rules above, include
one line near the top:

```
Follow: docs/milestone-loop-protocol.md
```

A milestone's `docs/m{N}-loop-prompts.md` should still spell out:

- the milestone's own scope, non-goals, and task list;
- per-Loop-Prompt read lists, scope, acceptance criteria;
- any **override** of a default in this file (e.g. a planning-only
  milestone overriding the worktree commit/push behavior).

---

## 7. Discovery / Debate Gate

_Added by M9.4. Additive only — §1–§6 above are unchanged._

Some tasks are large enough that "implement first, debate later"
loses load-bearing requirements (the canonical failure: `tools/legacy/kkr.py`
migration missing multi-Kaggle-account / owner / env semantics; see
`docs/meeting-notes/2026-05-24-r3.md` §6). The Discovery / Debate Gate
runs three role-isolated subagents — `legacy-archaeologist`,
`requirements-skeptic`, `design-red-team` — **before** any
implementation work begins.

The gate is **mandatory** for any task whose spec is tagged `arch:`
(introduces / revises an architectural primitive) or
`legacy-migration:` (migrates / rewrites / replaces a legacy artefact).
Routine tasks (bug fixes, doc edits, dependency bumps, small
refactors) do not trigger the gate.

When the gate fires, the executing session MUST:

1. Invoke `legacy-archaeologist` first if the task touches any
   legacy artefact (skip allowed only for greenfield `arch:` tasks,
   with explicit note in the closeout).
2. Invoke `requirements-skeptic` next.
3. Invoke `design-red-team` last.
4. Attach all three reports to the task closeout under
   `docs/evidence/<milestone>/<task>/discovery/`.
5. Verify all three canonical acceptance lines (defined in
   `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`) byte-for-byte
   against the reports. A missing acceptance line is a task FAIL.

Full template, tag-placement options, and the verbatim acceptance
lines live in `docs/architecture/discovery-debate-gate.md`. The
orchestration skill `.claude/skills/design-archaeology/SKILL.md`
(owned by M9.3) is the inline alternative when the task is small
enough not to warrant separate subagents; the agent path and the
skill path emit compatible output shapes by design.

M9.4 enforces the gate via task-spec acceptance criteria and this
section's wording, **not** via hook-level denials. Hook-based
enforcement is a deferred follow-up; file a separate issue if you
want it built.

````

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import nbformat

from percent_nb import (
    MagicFormatError,
    PercentFormatError,
    parse_percent_script,
    percent_cells_to_notebook_cells,
)

EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_RUNTIME = 1
EXIT_INPUT = 2
EXIT_FORMAT = 3


def _emit(
    args: argparse.Namespace, ok: bool, payload: dict[str, Any], exit_code: int
) -> int:
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps({"ok": ok, **payload}, ensure_ascii=False))
    elif ok:
        print(
            f"Wrote {payload['dst']} "
            f"({payload['written_cells']} cells; code={payload['code_cells']} markdown={payload['markdown_cells']})"
        )
    else:
        print(payload.get("message", "error"), file=sys.stderr)
    return exit_code


def build_notebook(src: Path, *, keep_markdown: bool) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, Any]]:
    text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    cells = parse_percent_script(text)
    nb = nbformat.v4.new_notebook()
    nb.cells = [
        nbformat.from_dict(cell)
        for cell in percent_cells_to_notebook_cells(
            cells, delete_markdown=not keep_markdown
        )
    ]
    nb.metadata.setdefault("language_info", {"name": "python"})
    code_cells = sum(1 for cell in nb.cells if cell.cell_type == "code")
    markdown_cells = sum(1 for cell in nb.cells if cell.cell_type == "markdown")
    summary = {
        "written_cells": len(nb.cells),
        "code_cells": code_cells,
        "markdown_cells": markdown_cells,
        "keep_markdown": keep_markdown,
    }
    return nb, summary


def _parse_bool_arg(value: str) -> bool:
    text = str(value).strip().lower()
    if text in {"1", "true", "t", "yes", "y", "on"}:
        return True
    if text in {"0", "false", "f", "no", "n", "off"}:
        return False
    raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"expected true/false, got: {value!r}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="py2nb.py",
        description="Convert a percent-v1 Python script into a Jupyter notebook.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("src", help="source python file")
    parser.add_argument(
        "dst", nargs="?", help="destination notebook path; default: <src>.ipynb"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--keep-markdown",
        type=_parse_bool_arg,
        default=False,
        metavar="BOOL",
        help="keep markdown cells in the generated notebook (default: false)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check",
        action="store_true",
        help="do not write, only report whether output would change",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--json", action="store_true", help="print machine-readable JSON to stdout"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        src = Path(args.src).expanduser().resolve()
        if not src.exists() or src.suffix.lower() != ".py":
            return _emit(
                args,
                False,
                {
                    "error": "invalid_input",
                    "message": f"source python file not found: {src}",
                },
                EXIT_INPUT,
            )
        dst = (
            Path(args.dst).expanduser().resolve()
            if args.dst
            else src.with_suffix(".ipynb")
        )
        nb, summary = build_notebook(src, keep_markdown=bool(args.keep_markdown))
        changed = True
        if dst.exists():
            try:
                with dst.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    current = nbformat.read(fh, as_version=4)
                changed = nbformat.writes(current) != nbformat.writes(nb)
            except Exception:
                changed = True
        if not args.check:
            dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with dst.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                nbformat.write(nb, fh)
        result = {
            "src": str(src),
            "dst": str(dst),
            "changed": changed,
            "check_only": bool(args.check),
            **summary,
        }
        return _emit(args, True, result, EXIT_OK)
    except (PercentFormatError, MagicFormatError) as exc:
        return _emit(
            args, False, {"error": "format_error", "message": str(exc)}, EXIT_FORMAT
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        return _emit(
            args, False, {"error": "runtime_error", "message": str(exc)}, EXIT_RUNTIME
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

```python
def test_nb_to_ipynb_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    src = tmp_path / "src.py"
    src.write_text(
        "# %% [markdown]\n# Hello\n\n# %%\nx = 1\nprint('hi', x)\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    dst = tmp_path / "out.ipynb"
    proc = _run(
        "nb", "to-ipynb", str(src), "--output", str(dst), "--keep-markdown", "--json"
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    payload = _parse_json(proc)
    assert payload["ok"] is True
    assert payload["side_effect"] == "LOCAL_WRITE"
    assert dst.exists()


def test_nb_to_py_roundtrip(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    # Make an ipynb via to-ipynb first.
    src = tmp_path / "src.py"
    src.write_text("# %% [markdown]\n# Hi\n\n# %%\nx = 2\n", encoding="utf-8")
    ipynb = tmp_path / "round.ipynb"
    p1 = _run(
        "nb", "to-ipynb", str(src), "--output", str(ipynb), "--keep-markdown", "--json"
    )
    assert p1.returncode == 0

    out_py = tmp_path / "round.py"
    p2 = _run("nb", "to-py", str(ipynb), "--output", str(out_py), "--json")
    assert p2.returncode == 0, p2.stderr
    payload = _parse_json(p2)
    assert payload["ok"] is True
    assert out_py.exists()
    assert "x = 2" in out_py.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
```

```python
"""kca DB access layer (psycopg3, sync).

Side-effect classification:
  - Operations against a local Supabase stack are LOCAL_WRITE.
  - Operations against a remote Postgres are REMOTE_WRITE and require
    both KCA_DB_TARGET=remote and KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE=1.

Env contract (set in .env, loaded automatically via python-dotenv if installed):
  - SUPABASE_DB_URL         : libpq conninfo string (preferred).
  - KCA_DB_TARGET           : "local" (default) or "remote".
  - KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE        : "1" to allow remote/submission operations.
  - SUPABASE_DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/DB : fallback discrete vars.

See env.example in the repo root for the full template.

Module is importable without a live DB — connections happen lazily.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterable

# Load .env from repo root automatically if python-dotenv is installed.
# This is a no-op when .env doesn't exist or dotenv isn't installed.
try:
    from dotenv import load_dotenv as _load_dotenv

    _load_dotenv(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / ".env", override=False)
except ImportError:
    pass

try:
    import psycopg
    from psycopg import sql  # noqa: F401  # re-exported for callers
    from psycopg.rows import dict_row
except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover
    psycopg = None  # type: ignore
    _import_err = e
else:
    _import_err = None

from _types import SideEffect
```

```python
def test_kca_kaggle_submit_refuses_without_credentials(tmp_path):
    """The whole point of dry-run CI: even if a buggy worker tried to call
    ``kca kaggle submit``, it must refuse cleanly when KAGGLE_USERNAME or
    KAGGLE_KEY are absent — before any network or subprocess call to
    ``kaggle`` could happen.

    We run kca as a subprocess with a scrubbed env. We also disable dotenv
    autoloading via ``KCA_SKIP_DOTENV`` (defensive — see below) and point
    ``HOME`` at a clean tmp dir so any local ``~/.kaggle/kaggle.json``
    is not picked up by the kaggle library.
    """
    env = {
        # Start from a minimal env. We deliberately do NOT inherit
        # KAGGLE_USERNAME / KAGGLE_KEY / SUPABASE_DB_URL / KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE
        # from the parent process — the whole point is to assert the
        # gate fires under a creds-free CI shell.
        "PATH": os.environ.get("PATH", ""),
        "HOME": str(tmp_path),
        "PYTHONPATH": str(REPO_ROOT),
        # Belt-and-suspenders: tell dotenv-style loaders to ignore .env.
        # `tools/kca/db.py` uses python-dotenv with override=False, so an
        # explicitly absent KAGGLE_USERNAME in the subprocess env can
        # still be re-populated from a project-root .env file. We point
        # HOME away and additionally clear any candidate locations.
    }
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [
            sys.executable,
            str(REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "kca" / "kca.py"),
            "kaggle",
            "submit",
            "--competition",
            "spaceship-titanic",
            "--file",
            "/dev/null",
            "--message",
            "m9-e2e dry-run — must refuse",
            "--json",
        ],
        env=env,
        cwd=str(tmp_path),  # outside repo root → no .env auto-discovery
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    # The submit path returns ok=False with EXIT_RUNTIME when creds are
    # missing (see tools/kca/kg.py::cmd_submit lines 145–162).
    assert proc.returncode != 0, (
        f"expected non-zero exit when KAGGLE_USERNAME absent; "
        f"stdout={proc.stdout!r} stderr={proc.stderr!r}"
    )
    stdout = (proc.stdout or "").strip()
    assert stdout, f"empty stdout; stderr={proc.stderr!r}"
    payload = json.loads(stdout)
    assert payload["ok"] is False
    assert payload["side_effect"] == "SUBMISSION"
    assert "KAGGLE_USERNAME" in payload["error"] or "KAGGLE_KEY" in payload["error"], (
        f"expected credentials-gate refusal, got {payload!r}"
    )
```

```python
# As of M2-T004, `kca run` is DB-first. Tests that exercise it skip when no DB
# is configured. Set KCA_DB_TARGET=local + SUPABASE_DB_URL to enable them.
requires_db = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not (os.environ.get("KCA_DB_TARGET") and os.environ.get("SUPABASE_DB_URL")),
    reason="kca run tests need KCA_DB_TARGET=local + SUPABASE_DB_URL (M2-T004 DB-first).",
)


def _run(
    *argv: str, env: dict | None = None, cwd: Path | None = None
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    full_env = os.environ.copy()
    if env is not None:
        for k, v in env.items():
            if v is None:
                full_env.pop(k, None)
            else:
                full_env[k] = v
    return subprocess.run(
        [*KCA, *argv],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
        env=full_env,
        cwd=str(cwd or REPO_ROOT),
    )
```

```python
RUN_JOB = [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "run_job.py")]


def _env_clean(**overrides) -> dict:
    """Copy os.environ minus DB/Kaggle/API keys; apply overrides last."""
    env = os.environ.copy()
    for k in (
        "SUPABASE_DB_URL",
        "KCA_DB_TARGET",
        "KAGGLE_USERNAME",
        "KAGGLE_KEY",
        "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY",
        "KCA_ALLOW_REMOTE",
    ):
        env.pop(k, None)
    for k, v in overrides.items():
        if v is None:
            env.pop(k, None)
        else:
            env[k] = v
    return env
```

> ## Q3 — Why no submission appears on Kaggle, and the fix
> 
> **Root cause is now clear from the live Kaggle state.** Three findings:
> 
> 1. `kaggle competitions submissions -c tpu-getting-started` shows **zero** new submissions from our M10 pushes — the most recent submission is from 2024-12-20, none from May 2026.
> 2. `kaggle kernels list -m --search "petals"` lists only old 2024 kernels — **neither** of our newly-pushed kernels (`petals-baseline-tl`, `petals-baseline-transfer-learning`) appears.
> 3. `kaggle kernels status harrysun2006/petals-baseline-tl` returns **500 Server Error** for both kernel slugs.
> 
> What this means: the kernels were either silently rejected by Kaggle, or pushed-and-then-broken (papermill error for push #2; never-ran for push #1). And critically — **Kaggle only auto-creates a competition submission when a kernel with `competition_sources: ["<slug>"]` runs to *completion*.** Neither of our runs completed, so no submission was ever produced. The submission flow is:
> 
> ```
> kaggle kernels push  →  kernel exists  →  kernel runs successfully  →  Kaggle auto-submits
>                                           ↑ both pushes died here
> ```
> 
> **Fix (now possible):** the kernelspec bug is already patched in this PR (`tools/legacy/py2nb.py` + regenerated `baseline.ipynb`), so a fresh push should actually run. The flow:
> 1. Merge PR #40 (or cherry-pick the kernelspec fix).
> 2. Re-push under fresh human approval: `kca kaggle push --competition tpu-getting-started --notebook experiments/tpu-getting-started/baseline-tl/baseline.ipynb --message "M10 re-push: kernelspec fix"`.
> 3. Verify with `kaggle kernels list -m` that the kernel appears.
> 4. Watch with `kaggle kernels status <ref>` until `complete`.
> 5. Then `kaggle competitions submissions -c tpu-getting-started` will show the new submission with `publicScore`.
> 
> There's also a UX gotcha: `kernel-metadata.json` has `is_private: true`. Private kernels are only visible to you when logged in (and only with `-m` flag), and they should still produce a competition submission. If you want the kernel publicly viewable, set `is_private: false`. Either way, the submission appears on the competition leaderboard.
> 
> ## Q4 — Can KCA read the public LB score?
> 
> **No, not currently.** Inspection of `tools/kca/kg.py`:
> 
> - `kca kaggle` subcommands: `submit, push, upload, download, verify, watch, fetch, list`.
> - `cmd_watch` polls `kaggle kernels status` (run status only — no score).
> - `cmd_fetch` and `cmd_list` are **stubs** (return `_emit_stub`).
> - No code path parses `publicScore` from `kaggle competitions submissions` output, and no wrapper hits `kaggle competitions leaderboard`.
> 
> The raw data exists — `kaggle competitions submissions -c <comp>` returns a `publicScore` column in tabular form (you saw it above for the 2024 submissions). KCA just doesn't ingest it. This is why T006's regression assertion had to be relaxed: there was no automated path to populate `submissions.public_score`.
> 
> **Proposed fix (small, M11 candidate)** — add `kca kaggle score`:
> 
> ```
> kca kaggle score --competition tpu-getting-started --kernel-ref harrysun2006/petals-baseline-tl --json
>   → calls `kaggle competitions submissions -c <comp> --csv`
>   → matches the row by kernel ref or message
>   → writes the publicScore back to the submissions row (UPDATE submissions SET public_score=... WHERE external_submission_id=...)
>   → emits {ok, side_effect: READ_ONLY, public_score, submission_status, ...}
> ```
> 
> Then `kca kaggle watch` could call `score` automatically once the kernel reaches `complete`, closing the loop. This would also turn T006's relaxed LB assertion back into a strict one.
>

```python
REGRESSION_GUARD_PP = 0.10

# experiment_runs.id values (stable across DB recreations of the same seed).
BASELINE_RUN_ID = "830fc32f-2ea8-4309-9fa6-e9cd1e5877ec"
ALT_RUN_ID = "c3339154-944b-49aa-8322-f4a8607ad240"

# The single M10-T004 push's submissions row (push #1; see module docstring).
M10_T004_SUBMISSION_ID = "03b5d080-1c05-47d7-9be1-abdb2ea31aff"
COMPETITION_ID = "4c69e842-eade-41e4-9143-b5d3966a9578"


def _fetch_holdout_accuracy(cur, run_id: str) -> float | None:
    """Return recorded holdout_accuracy for an experiment_runs row, or None.

    Reads ``metrics->'holdout_accuracy'->>'value'`` — the shape written by
    the M2 metrics path (``tools/kca/db.py::record_metric``). Returns None
    when no row exists so the caller can distinguish "no seed data" (fresh
    CI DB) from "regression".
    """
    cur.execute(
        """
        SELECT (metrics->'holdout_accuracy'->>'value')::float AS holdout_accuracy
        FROM experiment_runs
        WHERE id = %s
        """,
        (run_id,),
    )
    row = cur.fetchone()
    if row is None:
        return None
    acc = row[0]
    assert acc is not None, (
        f"experiment_runs[{run_id!r}].metrics->'holdout_accuracy'->>'value' is NULL"
    )
    return float(acc)


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def m10_metrics():
    """Read all M10 regression evidence from the DB in one connection.

    Skips cleanly when any seed row (baseline run, alt run, M10-T004
    submission) is missing — e.g. against the live-db CI job's fresh
    postgres, which has migrations applied but no recorded M10 data.
    """
    import psycopg

    with psycopg.connect(os.environ["SUPABASE_DB_URL"]) as conn:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            baseline_acc = _fetch_holdout_accuracy(cur, BASELINE_RUN_ID)
            alt_acc = _fetch_holdout_accuracy(cur, ALT_RUN_ID)

            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT id, public_score, external_submission_id,
                       experiment_run_id, competition_id
                FROM submissions
                WHERE id = %s
                """,
                (M10_T004_SUBMISSION_ID,),
            )
            sub = cur.fetchone()

            # kernel_push-related audit trail. The worker did not emit a
            # dedicated ``kernel_push`` *event_type*; it tags the operation
            # inside event_data (tool / operation / target_op) across
            # tool_call / approval_pause / reviewer_abstain rows.
            cur.execute(
                """
                SELECT count(*) FROM agent_job_events
                WHERE event_data->>'operation' = 'kernel_push'
                   OR event_data->>'tool' = 'kernel_push'
                   OR event_data->>'target_op' = 'kernel_push'
                """
            )
            kernel_push_event_count = cur.fetchone()[0]

    missing = []
    if baseline_acc is None:
        missing.append(f"experiment_runs[{BASELINE_RUN_ID!r}]")
    if alt_acc is None:
        missing.append(f"experiment_runs[{ALT_RUN_ID!r}]")
    if sub is None:
        missing.append(f"submissions[{M10_T004_SUBMISSION_ID!r}]")
    if missing:
        pytest.skip(
            "M10 seed data not present in DB ("
            + ", ".join(missing)
            + "); regression assertions require a DB seeded by "
            "M10-T002/T004/T005"
        )

    return {
        "baseline_acc": baseline_acc,
        "alt_acc": alt_acc,
        "submission_id": sub[0],
        "public_score": sub[1],
        "external_submission_id": sub[2],
        "submission_experiment_run_id": sub[3],
        "submission_competition_id": sub[4],
        "kernel_push_event_count": kernel_push_event_count,
    }


@requires_db
def test_baseline_local_metric_clears_floor(m10_metrics):
    acc = m10_metrics["baseline_acc"]
    assert acc >= BASELINE_FLOOR, (
        f"baseline holdout_accuracy={acc:.6f} fell below M10 floor "
        f"{BASELINE_FLOOR}; do NOT lower the threshold — investigate the "
        "run first (task spec stop condition)"
    )


@requires_db
def test_alt_local_metric_within_regression_guard(m10_metrics):
    """RELAXED form of "alt >= baseline".

    M10-T005's EfficientNetB0 regressed ~3.4pp vs the MobileNetV2 baseline
    (0.3966 vs 0.4310), accepted as PASS-with-note (head still climbing at
    3 epochs). The hard guard is a >10pp unexplained drop, mirroring the
    M10-T005 acceptance criterion. A strict ``alt >= baseline`` assertion
    would contradict the human's accept-and-continue decision, so we assert
    the documented weaker form here.
    """
    baseline = m10_metrics["baseline_acc"]
    alt = m10_metrics["alt_acc"]
    drop = baseline - alt
    assert drop <= REGRESSION_GUARD_PP, (
        f"alt-backbone holdout_accuracy={alt:.6f} regressed "
        f"{drop * 100:.1f}pp below baseline {baseline:.6f}, exceeding the "
        f"{REGRESSION_GUARD_PP * 100:.0f}pp unexplained-regression guard; "
        "this is the M9 'CV scores diverge' rollback condition — re-run "
        "M10-T005, do NOT widen the guard"
    )


@requires_db
def test_real_push_submission_row_exists(m10_metrics):
    """RELAXED form of "public_score IS NOT NULL".

    M10-T004's approved push never produced a public LB score (push #1
    stalled QUEUED; approved re-push #2 hit a now-fixed missing-kernelspec
    bug). The documented deviation (follow-ups #34/#35) is: a submissions
    row exists for the push attempt with external_submission_id populated
    and public_score NULL. We assert that shape and explicitly document the
    NULL public_score rather than fail or trigger a new Kaggle push.
    """
    # The row exists and links to the baseline run + competition.
    assert str(m10_metrics["submission_experiment_run_id"]) == BASELINE_RUN_ID, (
        f"M10-T004 submission row does not link to the baseline run {BASELINE_RUN_ID}"
    )
    assert str(m10_metrics["submission_competition_id"]) == COMPETITION_ID, (
        "M10-T004 submission row competition_id mismatch"
    )
    # external_submission_id is populated (the kernel-version ref).
    ext = m10_metrics["external_submission_id"]
    assert ext, (
        "M10-T004 submission row has empty external_submission_id; the "
        "push attempt should have recorded the kernel-version ref"
    )
    # DOCUMENTED DEVIATION: public_score is NULL because no kernel run
    # completed. This is the human-accepted state, tracked by #34/#35.
    # Asserting it is NULL pins the known deviation so a future accidental
    # backfill (or a real LB score landing) flips this test and forces a
    # conscious update rather than silently masking the gap.
    assert m10_metrics["public_score"] is None, (
        "public_score is no longer NULL for the M10-T004 push — a real LB "
        "score may have landed; update this test and re-assert the "
        "0 < score <= 1 sanity bound (see follow-ups #34/#35)"
    )


@requires_db
def test_kernel_push_event_recorded(m10_metrics):
    count = m10_metrics["kernel_push_event_count"]
    assert count > 0, (
        "no agent_job_events row records a kernel_push-related event "
        "(event_data.operation / tool / target_op == 'kernel_push'); the "
        "M10-T004 worker push should have left an audit trail"
```

```python
def add_parsers(sub: argparse._SubParsersAction) -> None:
    kg = sub.add_parser("kaggle", help="Kaggle remote operations (gated)")
    kg_sub = kg.add_subparsers(dest="kaggle_cmd", required=True)

    p_submit = kg_sub.add_parser("submit", help="Submit to a competition (SUBMISSION)")
    p_submit.add_argument("--competition", required=True)
    p_submit.add_argument("--file", required=True)
    p_submit.add_argument("--message", required=True)
    p_submit.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_submit.set_defaults(func=cmd_submit)

    p_push = kg_sub.add_parser("push", help="Push a kernel (REMOTE_WRITE)")
    p_push.add_argument(
        "--kernel-dir",
        dest="kernel_dir",
        required=True,
        help="Directory containing kernel-metadata.json",
    )
    p_push.add_argument(
        "--dry-run",
        action="store_true",
        help="Validate kernel-metadata.json without uploading",
    )
    p_push.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_push.set_defaults(func=cmd_push)

    p_upload = kg_sub.add_parser("upload", help="Upload dataset (REMOTE_WRITE)")
    p_upload.add_argument("--path", required=True)
    p_upload.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_upload.set_defaults(func=cmd_upload)

    p_download = kg_sub.add_parser(
        "download", help="Download competition data (LOCAL_WRITE)"
    )
    p_download.add_argument("--competition", required=True)
    p_download.add_argument(
        "--path", default=None, help="Destination dir (default ./data/<competition>)"
    )
    p_download.add_argument(
        "--resume",
        action="store_true",
        help="Skip files whose sha256 matches manifest entry",
    )
    p_download.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_download.set_defaults(func=cmd_download)

    p_verify = kg_sub.add_parser(
        "verify", help="Verify a downloaded dataset against manifest.json"
    )
    p_verify.add_argument(
        "--path", required=True, help="Directory holding manifest.json"
    )
    p_verify.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_verify.set_defaults(func=cmd_verify)

    p_watch = kg_sub.add_parser("watch", help="Watch a kernel run (READ_ONLY)")
    p_watch.add_argument("--run", default=None, help="Legacy alias for --kernel")
    p_watch.add_argument(
        "--kernel", default=None, help="Kernel ref (user/slug) to poll status for"
    )
    p_watch.add_argument("--poll-seconds", dest="poll_seconds", type=int, default=30)
    p_watch.add_argument("--max-iterations", dest="max_iterations", type=int, default=1)
    p_watch.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_watch.set_defaults(func=cmd_watch)

    p_fetch = kg_sub.add_parser("fetch", help="Fetch run artifacts (READ_ONLY)")
    p_fetch.add_argument("--run", required=True)
    p_fetch.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_fetch.set_defaults(func=cmd_fetch)

    p_list = kg_sub.add_parser("list", help="List Kaggle runs (READ_ONLY)")
    p_list.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    p_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_list)
```

```python
def update_submission(
    submission_id: str,
    *,
    public_lb_score: float | None = None,
    status: str | None = None,
    submitted_at=None,
    conn: "psycopg.Connection | None" = None,
) -> None:
    """Update submission after Kaggle response."""
    fields: list[str] = []
    params: list[Any] = []
    if public_lb_score is not None:
        fields.append("public_lb_score = %s")
        params.append(public_lb_score)
    if status is not None:
        fields.append("status = %s")
        params.append(status)
    if submitted_at is not None:
        fields.append("submitted_at = %s")
        params.append(submitted_at)
    if not fields:
        return
    _with_conn(conn, _update_submission_m4, submission_id, fields, params)


def _update_submission_m4(
    conn: "psycopg.Connection",
    submission_id: str,
    fields: list[str],
    params: list[Any],
) -> None:
    set_clause = ", ".join(fields)
    params.append(submission_id)
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute(
            f"UPDATE submissions SET {set_clause} WHERE id = %s::uuid",
            params,
        )
    conn.commit()
```

```diff
@@ -1,2 +1,108 @@+def _parse_kaggle_submissions_csv(text: str) -> list[dict]:
+    """Parse the CSV output of `kaggle competitions submissions -c <c> --csv`.
+
+    Returns a list of dicts. The Kaggle CLI uses these CSV columns:
+    fileName,date,description,status,publicScore,privateScore.
+    Empty score cells become None.
+    """
+    import csv
+    import io
+
+    rows: list[dict] = []
+    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))
+    for row in reader:
+        for k in ("publicScore", "privateScore"):
+            v = row.get(k, "")
+            row[k] = float(v) if v not in (None, "", "null") else None
+        rows.append(row)
+    return rows
+
+
+def cmd_score(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
+    """Read the public LB score for a competition's submissions and optionally
+    write the matched row's publicScore back to a `submissions` row.
+
+    READ_ONLY against Kaggle (calls `kaggle competitions submissions --csv`).
+    LOCAL_WRITE against the DB when --update-db is given.
+    """
+    competition = args.competition
+    se = SideEffect.READ_ONLY
+
+    proc = subprocess.run(
+        ["kaggle", "competitions", "submissions", "-c", competition, "--csv"],
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+    )
+    if proc.returncode != 0:
+        return _emit_json(
+            {
+                "ok": False,
+                "side_effect": se.value,
+                "competition": competition,
+                "error": (proc.stderr or "kaggle submissions failed").strip(),
+            }
+        )
+
+    submissions = _parse_kaggle_submissions_csv(proc.stdout)
+
+    matched = submissions
+    if args.kernel_ref:
+        # Match the kernel slug ("user/slug" or just "slug") inside the description.
+        slug_part = args.kernel_ref.split("/")[-1].lower()
+        matched = [
+            r for r in matched if slug_part in (r.get("description", "") or "").lower()
+        ]
+    if args.message_filter:
+        needle = args.message_filter.lower()
+        matched = [
+            r for r in matched if needle in (r.get("description", "") or "").lower()
+        ]
+
+    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "ok": True,
+        "side_effect": se.value,
+        "competition": competition,
+        "match_count": len(matched),
+        "submissions": matched[: args.limit] if args.limit else matched,
+    }
+
+    if args.update_db and args.submission_id:
+        if not matched:
+            payload["ok"] = False
+            payload["error"] = (
+                f"no Kaggle submissions row matched filters for "
+                f"competition={competition!r}; refusing to update DB"
+            )
+            return _emit_json(payload)
+        top = matched[0]
+        public_score = top.get("publicScore")
+        status = (top.get("status") or "").strip() or None
+        try:
+            db.update_submission(
+                args.submission_id,
+                public_lb_score=public_score,
+                status=status,
+            )
+            # `public_score` (M10 column) is the canonical one the tests read;
+            # mirror the value there too (kept in sync with public_lb_score).
+            with db.get_conn() as conn:
+                with conn.cursor() as cur:
+                    cur.execute(
+                        "UPDATE submissions SET public_score = %s WHERE id = %s::uuid",
+                        (public_score, args.submission_id),
+                    )
+                conn.commit()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            payload["ok"] = False
+            payload["error"] = f"DB update failed: {exc!s}"
+            return _emit_json(payload)
+        payload["updated_submission_id"] = args.submission_id
+        payload["public_score"] = public_score
+        payload["matched_description"] = top.get("description")
+        payload["side_effect"] = SideEffect.LOCAL_WRITE.value
+
+    return _emit_json(payload)
+
```

```python
``data/tpu-getting-started/local-slice/{train,val}/*.tfrec`` and records the
resulting ``holdout_accuracy`` and ``macro_f1`` into ``experiment_runs`` via
``kca run record-metric``.

This is the LOCAL CV/holdout sanity gate — not the Kaggle kernel run. No Kaggle
```

```python
The script is LOCAL_WRITE (writes ``runs/tpu-getting-started/alt-backbone-v1/metrics.json``,
``cv_summary.json``, and `experiment_runs` rows).
"""
```

````markdown
# tpu-getting-started experiments

Deliberate, committed Kaggle-kernel artifacts for the **Petals to the Metal — Flower Classification on TPU** competition (`tpu-getting-started`).

## Layout

```
experiments/tpu-getting-started/
├── baseline-tl/          MobileNetV2 transfer-learning baseline (M10-T002)
│   ├── baseline.py           ← source of truth (percent-format Python)
│   ├── baseline.ipynb        ← derived from baseline.py via `kca nb to-ipynb`
│   └── kernel-metadata.json  ← Kaggle push manifest
└── alt-backbone-v1/      EfficientNetB0 single-axis variant (M10-T005)
    ├── baseline.py
    ├── baseline.ipynb
    └── kernel-metadata.json
```

## Workflow

`baseline.py` is the source of truth. Whenever you edit it, regenerate the notebook:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=tools/kca python3 tools/kca/kca.py nb to-ipynb \
  experiments/tpu-getting-started/baseline-tl/baseline.py \
  --output experiments/tpu-getting-started/baseline-tl/baseline.ipynb \
  --keep-markdown --json
```

Push to Kaggle (gated):

```bash
kca kaggle push --kernel-dir experiments/tpu-getting-started/baseline-tl --json
```

Read the public LB score back after the kernel run completes:

```bash
kca kaggle score --competition tpu-getting-started \
  --kernel-ref harrysun2006/petals-baseline-tl --json
```

## Transient run state

Local-training metrics, logs, and any non-committed artifacts live under `runs/tpu-getting-started/<run_id>/` (gitignored). Only the files in this directory are versioned.

````

```
def _resolve_kaggle_input_path() -> str | None:
    p = Path("/kaggle/input") / COMPETITION
    if p.exists():
        return str(p)
    return None


def _resolve_local_slice() -> str | None:
    # When this notebook is executed locally from the repo root.
    for candidate in [
        Path.cwd() / "data" / COMPETITION / "local-slice",
        Path("/home/harry/test/tt_pangu/.claude/worktrees/m10-petals-to-the-metal/data") / COMPETITION / "local-slice",
    ]:
        if candidate.exists():
            return str(candidate)
    return None


GCS_PATH = _resolve_gcs_path()
KAGGLE_INPUT_PATH = _resolve_kaggle_input_path()
LOCAL_SLICE_PATH = _resolve_local_slice()

if GCS_PATH:
    DATA_ROOT = GCS_PATH
    DATA_SUBDIR = f"tfrecords-jpeg-{IMAGE_SIZE[0]}x{IMAGE_SIZE[1]}"
    RUNTIME = "kaggle-tpu"
elif KAGGLE_INPUT_PATH:
    DATA_ROOT = KAGGLE_INPUT_PATH
    DATA_SUBDIR = f"tfrecords-jpeg-{IMAGE_SIZE[0]}x{IMAGE_SIZE[1]}"
    RUNTIME = "kaggle-gpu"
elif LOCAL_SLICE_PATH:
    DATA_ROOT = LOCAL_SLICE_PATH
    DATA_SUBDIR = ""  # local slice is already at the per-split level
    RUNTIME = "local-slice"
else:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "No data source resolved: not on Kaggle (GCS/input path absent) and no local slice present. "
        "Run scripts/m10_t002_download_slice.py (or equivalent) to stage a single train/val shard."
    )

print(f"runtime={RUNTIME} data_root={DATA_ROOT} subdir={DATA_SUBDIR!r}")

# %% [markdown]
# ## TFRecord decoding

# %%
LABELED_TFREC_FORMAT = {
    "image": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string),
    "class": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.int64),
}

UNLABELED_TFREC_FORMAT = {
    "image": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string),
    "id": tf.io.FixedLenFeature([], tf.string),
}


def decode_image(image_bytes):
    image = tf.image.decode_jpeg(image_bytes, channels=3)
    image = tf.image.resize(image, IMAGE_SIZE)
```

> Here are the answers for all three.
> 
> ## v2 — the failure
> 
> **v2's actual error** (from `kaggle kernels output harrysun2006/petals-baseline-tl` log earlier):
> 
> ```
> Exception encountered at "In [3]":
> RuntimeError: No data source resolved: not on Kaggle (GCS/input path absent)
> and no local slice present. Run scripts/m10_t002_download_slice.py
> (or equivalent) to stage a single train/val shard.
> ```
> 
> v2 was `enable_gpu: true, enable_tpu: false`. Cell 3 of the notebook tries three paths and **all three failed on a GPU kernel**:
> 
> 1. `kaggle_datasets.KaggleDatasets().get_gcs_path('tpu-getting-started')` — silently caught an exception (the import or call failed; the original code swallowed the message).
> 2. `/kaggle/input/tpu-getting-started/` — didn't exist. Even though `competition_sources: ["tpu-getting-started"]` is set in `kernel-metadata.json`, Kaggle does **not** auto-mount this competition's data under `/kaggle/input/` because Petals to the Metal stores data on GCS rather than as a standard Kaggle competition dataset.
> 3. Local slice (`data/tpu-getting-started/local-slice/`) — N/A on Kaggle.
> 
> So v2 ran for ~67s, hit the unresolved-data raise in cell 3, and Kaggle marked the run failed. **No submission was created** (auto-submit only fires when the kernel completes successfully).
> 
> ## v3 — fix to v2
> 
> Yes, v3 is the fix for v2. Three changes in v3 over v2:
> 
> | Field | v2 | v3 |
> |---|---|---|
> | `enable_gpu` | `true` | `false` |
> | `enable_tpu` | `false` | `true` |
> | Resolution code | swallowed exceptions silently | now `print(...)` on each failed branch + lists `/kaggle/input/*` if absent |
> 
> The intent: with TPU enabled, `kaggle_datasets.KaggleDatasets().get_gcs_path('tpu-getting-started')` returns a real GCS path (the canonical Petals to the Metal pattern — TPU is what the competition was designed around). The diagnostic prints mean that if v3 *also* fails to resolve, the log will tell us exactly why this time.
> 
> The notebook code (cells) is otherwise unchanged (same MobileNetV2 backbone, same training loop).
> 
> ## v3 — why pending ~17 min
> 
> Three plausible reasons:
> 
> 1. **TPU queue, not stall.** Kaggle TPU pool is small and high-demand. Petals-to-the-Metal TPU kernels routinely sit 5–20 min in queue before scheduling, especially in peak hours. ~17 min is at the high end of normal but not unprecedented.
> 2. **TPU weekly quota.** Kaggle gives ~30 hours/week of TPU time per user. Your account (`harrysun2006`) has many April-2026 `gpt-oss-120b-*` runs in its history — if any of those consumed TPU quota and the weekly window hasn't reset, new TPU kernels stay queued until reset.
> 3. **Status API trouble.** All 22 of my `kaggle kernels status` polls have returned **500 Server Error** for this slug — not just for v3. This was the same behavior for v1 (M10-T004 push #1, which never escaped QUEUED in 66 min). It's possible the slug has a backend issue with the status endpoint, masking the real state.
> 
> What I can tell you concretely right now (just re-checked):
> 
> - 22 polls, **all 500** — status API is broken for this slug.
> - `kaggle kernels output` returns **no log** → v3 has not terminated yet. (When v2 errored, the output API immediately returned the log.)
> - `kaggle competitions submissions` shows **no new row** — latest is still 2024-12-20 0.95106 → v3 hasn't auto-submitted yet.
> 
> The background poller keeps polling every 30s until either Kaggle returns a terminal status (`COMPLETE/ERROR/CANCEL`) or it hits the 30-min cap (≈13 more min). If v3 doesn't terminate by then and the status API stays broken, the most reliable check is `kaggle kernels output` — when that starts returning a fresh log, we'll know v3 is terminal regardless of what the status endpoint says.
> 
> If you want to rule out the quota theory now, you can check your TPU quota at https://www.kaggle.com/code in the right sidebar (it shows "X / 30 hours remaining this week"). If it's near zero, v3 will queue until the weekly reset (Saturday 00:00 UTC).

> 
> ## Diagnostic output (cell 3, data resolution)
> 
> ```
> [data-resolve] /kaggle/input contents: ['competitions']
> runtime=kaggle-tpu data_root=/kaggle/input/tpu-getting-started subdir='tfrecords-jpeg-192x192'
> train shards=0 train_images=0 val shards=0 val_images=0 steps_per_epoch=1
> strategy=default replicas=1
> ```
> 
> ## Problem 1 — data path is wrong (silent)
> 
> `kaggle_datasets.KaggleDatasets().get_gcs_path('tpu-getting-started')` returned `/kaggle/input/tpu-getting-started` (kaggle_datasets returns a local mount path when running on Kaggle infra). But that directory **doesn't exist** — the only thing under `/kaggle/input/` is `competitions/`. So the TFRecord enumeration found **0 train shards, 0 val shards**. The notebook proceeded silently with zero data, which is itself a bug — it should have failed loudly.
> 
> Real data is probably at `/kaggle/input/competitions/tpu-getting-started/tfrecords-jpeg-192x192/{train,val}/*.tfrec` (the structure for "official" Getting Started competitions). The resolver needs to check that path first.
> 
> ## Problem 2 — `enable_internet: false` blocks weight download (the actual failure)
> 
> Cell 7 errors with:
> 
> ```
> Exception encountered at "In [7]":
> Cell In[7], line 25
> ---> 25     model = build_model()
> ...
> URLError: <urlopen error [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution>
> Exception: URL fetch failure on https://storage.googleapis.com/tensorflow/keras-applications/mobilenet_v2/...weights...h5
> ```
> 
> `tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(weights="imagenet")` tries to download the ImageNet pretrained weights from `storage.googleapis.com`. With `enable_internet: false`, DNS resolution is blocked, so the download fails.
> 
> ## Fix plan (one more push needed)
> 
> 1. **Set `enable_internet: true`** in `kernel-metadata.json`. For Petals to the Metal this is allowed by the competition rules — many top notebooks use it.
> 2. **Fix the data-resolver** to also check `/kaggle/input/competitions/<slug>/` before giving up, and raise loudly if the resolved path contains 0 shards (instead of silently training on nothing).
> 
> These are local changes to `baseline.py` + `kernel-metadata.json` (no DB or external write). Then one more push.
>

```python
        raise RuntimeError(f"No TFRecords found for split={split} glob={_split_glob(split)}")
    ds = tf.data.TFRecordDataset(files, num_parallel_reads=tf.data.AUTOTUNE)
    ds = ds.with_options(tf.data.Options())
    ds = ds.map(
        read_labeled_tfrecord if labeled else read_unlabeled_tfrecord,
        num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE,
    )
    return ds


def get_training_dataset():
    ds = load_dataset("train", labeled=True)
    ds = ds.repeat()
```

```bash
  echo "[$ts poll $i] log_size=$log_size newest=$newest" >> .agent/audit/kernel_v4_poll/poll.log
  if [ "$log_size" -gt 100 ]; then
    echo "[$ts poll $i] TERMINAL: log populated ($log_size bytes)"
    break
  fi
  if echo "$newest" | grep -q "^2026-06"; then
    echo "[$ts poll $i] TERMINAL: new 2026-06 submission: $newest"
    break
  fi
  sleep 60
done
echo "---final state---"
tail -3 .agent/audit/kernel_v4_poll/poll.log
```

```diff
+            max_minutes=getattr(args, "max_poll_minutes", 60),

+        response["ok"] = push_ok and watch_result.get("terminal", False)

+
+def _watch_kernel_until_terminal(
+    kernel_ref: str, *, poll_seconds: int = 60, max_minutes: int = 60
+) -> dict:
+    """Poll a kernel run until it produces a downloadable output log.
+
+    Returns a dict with: terminal (bool), polls, runtime_seconds, log_path,
+    error_excerpt (if a Python traceback is detected in stderr). The Kaggle
+    `kernels status` API has been observed to 500 for newly-pushed kernels;
+    this watcher uses `kernels output` instead, which only succeeds once the
+    run is terminal.
+
+    READ_ONLY against Kaggle.
+    """
+    import os as _os
+    import time as _time
+    import tempfile
+
+    tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="kca-watch-")
+    log_path = Path(tmp_dir) / f"{kernel_ref.split('/')[-1]}.log"
+    polls = 0
+    started = _time.monotonic()
+    max_polls = max(1, (max_minutes * 60) // poll_seconds)
+    while polls < max_polls:
+        polls += 1
+        try:
+            if log_path.exists():
+                log_path.unlink()
+        except OSError:
+            pass
+        # `kaggle kernels output` exits 1 + writes nothing while running;
+        # exits 0 + writes log file once terminal.
+        subprocess.run(
+            ["kaggle", "kernels", "output", kernel_ref, "-p", tmp_dir],
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        )
+        if log_path.exists() and log_path.stat().st_size > 100:
+            break
+        if polls < max_polls:
+            _time.sleep(poll_seconds)
+
+    runtime = _time.monotonic() - started
+    terminal = log_path.exists() and log_path.stat().st_size > 100
+    result: dict = {
+        "terminal": terminal,
+        "polls": polls,
+        "runtime_seconds": round(runtime, 1),
+        "log_path": str(log_path) if terminal else None,
+    }
+
+    if terminal:
+        # Extract any "Exception encountered" / Traceback excerpt so the caller
+        # (auto-fix loop or human) can see the failure mode without re-reading
+        # the full multi-MB log.
+        try:
+            entries = json.loads(log_path.read_text())
+            stderr_lines = [
+                r["data"]
+                for r in entries
+                if r.get("stream_name") == "stderr"
+                and "Traceback" in r.get("data", "")
+            ]
+            error_window = []
+            if stderr_lines:
+                # Capture the last ~30 stderr lines starting from the traceback
+                tail_start = next(
+                    (i for i, r in enumerate(entries) if "Traceback" in r.get("data", "")),
+                    -1,
+                )
+                if tail_start >= 0:
+                    error_window = [
+                        r["data"].rstrip()
+                        for r in entries[tail_start : tail_start + 60]
+                        if r.get("stream_name") == "stderr"
+                    ]
+            result["error_excerpt"] = "\n".join(error_window[-30:]) if error_window else None
+        except Exception as exc:
+            result["error_excerpt"] = f"<log parse failed: {exc!r}>"
+
+    return result
```

```python
# ## Resolve data paths
#
# Try Kaggle's GCS-backed dataset path first (kernel runner). Fall back to the local M10-T002 slice.


# %%
def _resolve_gcs_path() -> str | None:
    try:
        from kaggle_datasets import KaggleDatasets  # type: ignore

        return KaggleDatasets().get_gcs_path(COMPETITION)
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"[data-resolve] kaggle_datasets GCS path unavailable: {exc!r}")
        return None


def _resolve_kaggle_input_path() -> str | None:
    # Try the direct competition mount first, then the /competitions/<slug>/ layout
    # Kaggle uses for "official" Getting Started competitions (v3 diagnostic showed
    # /kaggle/input had only ['competitions'], not the slug directly).
    candidates = [
        Path("/kaggle/input") / COMPETITION,
        Path("/kaggle/input/competitions") / COMPETITION,
    ]
    for p in candidates:
        if p.exists():
            print(f"[data-resolve] /kaggle/input mount found at {p}")
            return str(p)
    # Diagnostic: list what IS under /kaggle/input/ so a future failure shows
    # the real layout instead of an opaque "not found".
    root = Path("/kaggle/input")
    if root.exists():
        try:
            print(
                f"[data-resolve] /kaggle/input contents: {sorted(p.name for p in root.iterdir())}"
            )
            comp_root = root / "competitions"
            if comp_root.exists():
                print(
                    f"[data-resolve] /kaggle/input/competitions contents: "
                    f"{sorted(p.name for p in comp_root.iterdir())}"
                )
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"[data-resolve] /kaggle/input listdir failed: {exc!r}")
    else:
        print("[data-resolve] /kaggle/input does not exist")
    return None


def _resolve_local_slice() -> str | None:
    # When this notebook is executed locally from the repo root.
    for candidate in [
        Path.cwd() / "data" / COMPETITION / "local-slice",
        Path("/home/harry/test/tt_pangu/.claude/worktrees/m10-petals-to-the-metal/data")
        / COMPETITION
        / "local-slice",
    ]:
        if candidate.exists():
            return str(candidate)
    return None


GCS_PATH = _resolve_gcs_path()
KAGGLE_INPUT_PATH = _resolve_kaggle_input_path()
LOCAL_SLICE_PATH = _resolve_local_slice()

if GCS_PATH:
    DATA_ROOT = GCS_PATH
    DATA_SUBDIR = f"tfrecords-jpeg-{IMAGE_SIZE[0]}x{IMAGE_SIZE[1]}"
    RUNTIME = "kaggle-tpu"
elif KAGGLE_INPUT_PATH:
    DATA_ROOT = KAGGLE_INPUT_PATH
    DATA_SUBDIR = f"tfrecords-jpeg-{IMAGE_SIZE[0]}x{IMAGE_SIZE[1]}"
    RUNTIME = "kaggle-gpu"
elif LOCAL_SLICE_PATH:
    DATA_ROOT = LOCAL_SLICE_PATH
    DATA_SUBDIR = ""  # local slice is already at the per-split level
    RUNTIME = "local-slice"
else:
    raise RuntimeError(
        "No data source resolved: not on Kaggle (GCS/input path absent) and no local slice present. "
        "Run scripts/m10_t002_download_slice.py (or equivalent) to stage a single train/val shard."
    )

print(f"runtime={RUNTIME} data_root={DATA_ROOT} subdir={DATA_SUBDIR!r}")
```

```
(file_name: str, message: str, competition: Optional[str] = None, kernel: Optional[str] = None, kernel_version: Optional[int] = None, quiet: bool = False) -> kagglesdk.competitions.types.competition_api_service.ApiCreateCodeSubmissionResponse

    def competition_submit_code(
        self,
        file_name: str,
        message: str,
        competition: Optional[str] = None,
        kernel: Optional[str] = None,
        kernel_version: Optional[int] = None,
        quiet: bool = False,
    ) -> ApiCreateCodeSubmissionResponse:
        """Submit to a code competition.

        Args:
            file_name (str): the name of  the output file created by the kernel (not used for packages)
            message (str): the submission description
            competition (Optional[str]): the competition name; if not given use the 'competition' config value
            kernel (Optional[str]): the <owner>/<notebook> of the notebook to use for a code competition
            kernel_version (Optional[int]): the version number, returned by 'kaggle kernels push ...'
            quiet (bool): suppress verbose output (default is False)

        Returns:
            ApiCreateCodeSubmissionResponse:
        """
        if competition is None:
            competition = self.get_config_value(self.CONFIG_NAME_COMPETITION)
            if competition is not None and not quiet:
                print("Using competition: " + competition)
        if competition is None:
            raise ValueError("No competition specified")

        if kernel is None:
            raise ValueError("No kernel specified")
        else:
            with self.build_kaggle_client() as kaggle:
                items = kernel.split("/")
                if len(items) != 2:
                    raise ValueError("The kernel must be specified as <owner>/<notebook>")
                submit_request = ApiCreateCodeSubmissionRequest()
                submit_request.file_name = file_name
                submit_request.competition_name = competition
                submit_request._kernel_owner = items[0]
                submit_request.kernel_slug = items[1]
                if kernel_version:
                    submit_request.kernel_version = int(kernel_version)
```

```python
def test_db_unreachable_degrades_gracefully(cleanup_run_dir: str) -> None:
    """M4: run init is FS-first; DB failure becomes a warning, FS still wins."""
    slug = cleanup_run_dir
    proc = _run(
        "run",
        "init",
        "--competition",
        slug,
        "--json",
        env_override={
            "SUPABASE_DB_URL": "postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54998/postgres"
        },
    )
    assert proc.returncode == 0, proc.stderr
    payload = _parse(proc)
    assert payload["ok"] is True
    assert payload.get("db_warning"), "DB failure should surface as db_warning"
    # FS state still created (relative to the worker's cwd = REPO_ROOT).
    assert (REPO_ROOT / payload["run_dir"] / "meta.json").exists()


@requires_db
```

```bash
## Changes

### Q1 — Switch to cloud Supabase
- `tools/kca/db.py` auto-loads `.vscode/.env` with `override=True` (workspace DSN beats stale parent shell env) and `~/repo/.env` with `override=False` (fallback). Keeps the `KCA_SKIP_DOTENV` opt-out from issue #11.
- `tests/conftest.py::db_url` mirrors the same resolution.
- `tests/test_kca_db_smoke.py::test_db_unreachable_degrades_gracefully`, `tests/test_m5_smoke.py::_env_clean`, `tests/test_m6_smoke.py::_env_clean` now set `KCA_SKIP_DOTENV=1` in their scrubbed envs so the degradation/no-db tests stay green when `.vscode/.env` is present.
- All 7 supabase/migrations applied to cloud (PG 17.6, `aws-1-ap-northeast-2.pooler.supabase.com`).

### Q2 — Notebook artifacts moved to `experiments/`
- `runs/tpu-getting-started/{baseline-tl,alt-backbone-v1}/{baseline.py,baseline.ipynb,kernel-metadata.json}` → `experiments/tpu-getting-started/...`.
- `runs/` stays gitignored for transient run state (metrics, logs).
- `experiments/tpu-getting-started/README.md` documents the workflow.

### Q3 — Kaggle push landed an LB score
Iterated v3→v4→v5 within the user's auto-fix streak guards. Each push tagged at the exact commit it was pushed from:
| Tag | Commit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `kaggle/petals-baseline-tl/v3` | `28dc743` | ❌ URLError (internet blocked weight download) |
| `kaggle/petals-baseline-tl/v4` | `3812c5e` | ❌ Zero TFRecords (fail-loud caught GCS shortcut bug) |
| `kaggle/petals-baseline-tl/v5` | `cc8cfab` | ✅ holdout 0.7632, LB **0.76505** |
- v4 fix: `enable_internet=true`, added `/kaggle/input/competitions/<slug>/` candidate, fail-loud on 0 shards.
- v5 fix: validate each resolver's returned path actually contains `<subdir>/train` before accepting it (the GCS resolver returns a "shortcut" path on TPU that does NOT contain the data — silent failure caught here).

### Q4 — `kca kaggle score` + auto-watch on push
- `kca kaggle score --competition <c> [--kernel-ref ...] [--message-filter ...] [--submission-id ... --update-db]` parses `kaggle.api.competition_submissions` and (optionally) writes `public_score` + `public_lb_score` back to a `submissions` row.
- `kca kaggle push` now auto-polls `kaggle kernels output` until the run is terminal (`--no-watch` to opt out, `--poll-seconds` and `--max-poll-minutes` configurable). Returns `watch.terminal`, `watch.polls`, `watch.runtime_seconds`, `watch.log_path`, and a `watch.error_excerpt` when a Traceback is detected — primed for the auto-fix loop's next iteration.

## Tests

- Full suite vs cloud Supabase: **112 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed**.
- `ruff check .` clean. `ruff format --check` clean on changed files.
- Smoke-verified end-to-end: `kca kaggle push experiments/tpu-getting-started/baseline-tl --watch` → push → poll → kernel run → submission via `competition_submit_code` → `kca kaggle score --update-db` → `submissions.public_score = 0.76505`.

## Remote side effects

- Three real `kaggle kernels push` calls (v3/v4/v5) under the user's explicit approval. Single Notebook-competition submission via `competition_submit_code` (Petals to the Metal does not accept direct CSV uploads; this is the canonical path).
- Cloud Supabase: 7 migrations applied; one competition row, one submissions row written (the `tpu-getting-started` regression record).

## Tag policy

Going forward, each kernel push gets `git tag kaggle/<owner>/<slug>/v{N}` at the commit it was pushed from. v3/v4/v5 tags pushed alongside this PR.
```

```bash
### Re: ruff lint failure
Fixed in `97f6949` — applied `ruff format` to the two alt-backbone-v1 files. The notebook was regenerated from the formatted `.py` source. Local sweep is green; pushed CI run is in flight.

### Re: KCA goal-driven workflow + smart polling + parallel exploration

These are great directions for the next milestone (M11+). I'd like to file each bullet as a tracked issue so the work has a paper trail rather than living only in this PR comment. Concretely:

1. **Goal setting at start of competition** (e.g. "target top-10 LB by date X") — KCA reads competition rules + leaderboard percentiles, writes a `goal.md` per competition, validates each candidate against it before pushing. → new issue, `area:kaggle area:agent-sdk priority:P1`.

2. **Parallel exploration with local GPU screening** — multiple candidate experiments fan out under `experiments/<comp>/<run-id>/`, each fitting locally first (GPU/CPU); only the best-by-CV graduate to a Kaggle push. → new issue, `area:worker area:kaggle priority:P1`.

3. **Multi-push concurrency within Kaggle's per-competition rules** — auto-detect the limit (`competition_view` gives `max_daily_submissions` + concurrency hint; defaults to 2 queued + 1 running unless the competition page says otherwise) and respect it. → new issue, `area:kaggle priority:P1`.

4. **Smart polling: Fibonacci / Exponential backoff with `max_interval = 1/3 × estimated_queue_time`, switch to ~5-min stable interval once RUNNING** — change `_watch_kernel_until_terminal()` to read the kernel status field (when not 500'd), classify QUEUED vs RUNNING, and pick the cadence. Fall back to the current fixed-cadence path when status is unavailable. → new issue, `area:kaggle priority:P1`.

5. **Batched status query for many concurrent kernels** — single `kaggle kernels list -m` parse + per-slug match, instead of N parallel `kernels status` calls. Aligns naturally with #4. → bundled into #4's issue.

6. **Auto-continue after success until goal hit** — on successful submission, if `LB < goal`, KCA reads its own history (`submissions` rows) + Kaggle forum posts / public notebooks / GitHub for new ideas, drafts the next experiment, runs the same fan-out. → bundled into #1/#2.

7. **Human-in-the-loop escalation when stuck** — if no further idea after exhausting the search budget, KCA writes a status report (current LB, deltas tried, parameters explored, sources consulted) and opens an `ai:blocked decision:needed` issue summarizing the dead-end + asking for direction. The existing `human_decisions` table + Approval Inbox is the natural surface; just needs the "stuck" trigger + report template. → new issue, `area:agent-sdk area:ui priority:P1`.

Will you let me know if you want me to file these issues now (each gated `ai:triage` for your review before they're picked up), or capture them in a single design doc (e.g. `docs/adr/00XX-goal-driven-kaggle-loop.md`) for review before splitting into work items?
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3
```

```
=== milestones.md head ===
# kaggle-code-agent Milestones

Status: M0–M10 done; M9.2 ✓ done (/save-log operator-tooling skill); M11 in planning (authorized CTF/lab workflow)  
Created: 2026-05-16  
Scope: hybrid human + AI code competition platform

## Product thesis

`kaggle-code-agent` is a platform for human users to collaborate with AI code agents on code competitions and authorized challenge environments.

Initial focus: Kaggle competitions.  
Later extensions: authorized CTF/lab challenges, Devpost, hackathons, benchmark competitions, and other policy-scoped coding contests.

The platform should help a human user:

- discuss ideas and strategies;
- research competition rules, data, notebooks, papers, discussions, and baseline approaches;
- create, modify, test, and iterate code;
- track experiments, artifacts, results, submissions, and analysis;
- require human approval for external side effects such as Kaggle submissions or remote kernel pushes;
- summarize learnings and produce final writeups.

## Source of truth

**GitHub repo + Claude Code + CI + Supabase migrations.**

All product source code, migrations, tests, architecture decisions, and task specs live in this repository. AI tools do not share hidden memory reliably across sessions or products. Claude Code is the primary development environment for all layers: CLI, backend, UI shell, and worker.

Lovable may be used for visual prototyping or landing-page mockups only. It is not the source of truth for schema, migrations, agent runners, or any backend logic.

## Terminology: two meanings of "code agent"

This project uses two related but distinct agent concepts.

### 1. Platform-development coding agents

These are external AI tools used to build this repository.

Examples:

- Claude Code CLI / VS Code / Desktop / Web (primary);
- ChatGPT Pro / Cursor (supplementary);
- GitHub Actions / Claude Code Web / Routines for cloud automation.

Role:

- write and review this product's source code;
- update docs, tasks, tests, and architecture decisions;
- run local tests and CI repair loops;
- open branches/PRs under human supervision.

Important rule: these tools do not share hidden memory reliably. GitHub repository files are the durable source of truth.

### 2. Runtime competition code agents

These are agents launched by the finished platform to help a human user compete.

Initial runtime direction:

- Claude Agent SDK as the first core worker/harness;
```

````bash
$ gh issue create --title "feat(kaggle): goal-driven workflow — set per-competition goal + validate candidates against it" \
  --label "type:feature,ai:triage,area:kaggle,area:agent-sdk,priority:P1" \
  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Context

Surfaced in PR #44 (M10 follow-up). After the first end-to-end LB landed (0.76505 on Petals to the Metal, well below the user's notional "top 10" expectation), the workflow has no concept of a target. The agent pushed once and stopped — there's no mechanism for "iterate until goal hit" or "give up gracefully when no further idea."

## Proposed design

A new artefact: `goal.md` per competition (committed alongside `experiments/<comp>/`), with fields like:

```yaml
target_lb_rank: 10
target_lb_score: 0.92    # optional concrete floor
deadline: 2026-08-01
exit_strategy: human-in-the-loop-when-stuck
```

Workflow integration:

1. `kca competition register` (or a new `kca goal init`) prompts for goal + writes `goal.md`.
2. Every Kaggle push validates the candidate against the goal before submitting (CV/holdout >= some heuristic % of `target_lb_score`).
3. Successful submissions trigger a goal-check; if `LB < target`, KCA proposes the next experiment automatically (paired with #file_with_parallel_exploration_issue_link).
4. Goal status surfaces in the Approval Inbox / kca run list output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `goal.md` schema + `kca goal {init,show,update}` subcommands.
- [ ] `submissions` table grows a nullable FK to a `goals` table (so a future LB read can compute "% of goal").
- [ ] Reviewer gate consults `goal.md` and surfaces `goal_remaining_delta` in the approval request.
- [ ] A failing-to-converge state is detected (N submissions without monotone improvement) and triggers the human-in-the-loop escalation issue.

## Related

- PR #44 comment thread: https://github.com/amyteq/tt_pangu/pull/44#issuecomment-4654696548
- Pairs with #parallel-exploration, #multi-push-concurrency, #smart-polling, #human-in-the-loop
- Will land in M14 (planned post-M13).
EOF

  --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Context

Surfaced in PR #44 (M10 follow-up). M10 demonstrated ONE candidate pushed serially. The agent should explore N candidates in parallel, fit each locally first (GPU/CPU), and only graduate the best-by-CV to a Kaggle push.

## Proposed design

1. **Candidate fan-out**: a new orchestrator (e.g. `kca explore` or worker harness) takes a base notebook + a tiny "search space" YAML (`backbone ∈ {MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0, ResNet50}`, `image_size ∈ {192, 224, 331}`, `mixup ∈ {0, 0.2}`) and writes one `experiments/<comp>/<run-id>/` per cell of the cross-product (or a small random sample).
2. **Local screening loop**: each candidate runs `scripts/<comp>_local_train.py` with the local slice and records `holdout_accuracy` + `train_seconds` into `experiment_runs`.
3. **Candidate ranking**: a `kca explore rank` command queries `experiment_runs` for the run set, prints sorted by holdout, and the top K can be promoted to Kaggle push.
4. **Resource gating**: optional `--max-concurrent` and a check on local GPU memory before fanning out.
5. **Idea-sourcing extension** (paired with #goal-driven-workflow): when LB < goal, KCA reads competition forum posts / top public kernels / arxiv + drafts the NEXT batch of candidates rather than just stopping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `experiments/<comp>/<run-id>/` directories generated mechanically from a search-space spec.
- [ ] N candidates trainable in parallel locally (process pool + GPU memory check).
- [ ] `kca explore rank --competition <c>` lists candidates by holdout / macro_f1.
- [ ] Idea-sourcing step writes a `next_candidates.yaml` proposal that the user can edit/approve.
- [ ] Telemetry: a `experiment_runs.analysis.exploration_batch_id` link so an "exploration cohort" is queryable.

## Related

- PR #44 comment thread: https://github.com/amyteq/tt_pangu/pull/44#issuecomment-4654696548
- Pairs with #goal-driven-workflow, #multi-push-concurrency, #smart-polling

EOF
````
